role: role-separated security exposure and access advisory agent

findings.claim: The design cleanly separates 11 exact-PDF entries from 33 landing-page resolution entries, assigns the latter to a distinct metadata_url_resolver role and keeps both phases proposed and unauthorized.
findings.uncertainty: The 33 exact PDF URLs remain unknowable until separately authorized access to the official landing pages; no request was made in this review.
findings.remediation: Authorize and receipt only the 33-page resolution phase, then freeze and return the resolved exact-PDF manifest before any newly resolved PDF request.

findings.claim: Access receipts now dereference role, authority, input and tool artifacts; require nonempty access and output evidence; derive the exact canonical URL allowlist from the bound role-specific resolution or acquisition manifest; enforce output confinement and digests; and support exact role rosters with distinct sessions. Capacity receipts bind the resource plan and private-staging, network-sandbox and parser-sandbox artifacts.
findings.uncertainty: Receipts prove recorded artifacts and process claims, not absence of model pretraining knowledge or unrecorded access outside an enforced sandbox.
findings.remediation: At execution, require the network and parser sandboxes to enforce the same manifest-derived allowlist and resource policy, and validate chronological ordering of receipt timestamps.

findings.claim: Structural records carry acquisition, binary-security, access, authority and telemetry digests; merged eligibility binds each record to the frozen frame and policies and now requires every rank in the inspected prefix exactly once before deterministic selection.
findings.uncertainty: The structural record stores linked receipt digests without paths, and selection currently verifies the record and frame but does not independently dereference those acquisition, scan, access, authority and telemetry receipts.
findings.remediation: Before structural evidence is accepted, add or operate a verifier that resolves every linked digest, proves source-digest continuity and role identity, and recomputes telemetry under the frozen scanner contract.

findings.claim: The comparator now authenticates an externally supplied owner-authorization artifact, its bindings through both primary-only extractor bundles and access receipts, a recorded access event for that authority input, the sealed 24-primary plus six-reserve selection, both extraction runs, source-file digests, distinct sessions, exact contract and row schema, fixed semantic vocabulary and exact 24-key identity scope before concordance.
findings.uncertainty: The comparator now recomputes the sealed selection from its bound eligibility receipt and policy, but the caller-supplied packet SHA is not dereferenced to a packet artifact. Process receipts also cannot by themselves prove that declared sandbox controls operated outside the recorded evidence.
findings.remediation: Before a passing result is accepted, bind packet identity through a path-plus-digest artifact rather than an unverified digest string and require the operating sandbox to emit independently verifiable enforcement telemetry.

findings.claim: The general HTTP client remains the final hard pre-access blocker because it does not consume the bound authorization and URL manifest and does not validate every redirect hop and connection-time public-network destination before connection.
findings.uncertainty: No live request, redirect, DNS-rebinding or hostile-document test was performed because all source access remains prohibited.
findings.remediation: Implement an exact decision-and-manifest-bound client or sandbox proxy with pre-connect hop validation, connection-time public-IP enforcement, bounded redirects, retries and aggregate budgets, private non-Git custody, content-type and file-magic checks, and adversarial redirect, rebinding and hostile-document tests.

findings.claim: All source-resolution, acquisition, opening, inspection, extraction, contact, rights, publication, release and G2 authority states remain false; the design builder and this review perform no network operation.
findings.uncertainty: A reproducible no-access design is not evidence that future network, sandbox, custody or extraction controls have operated successfully.
findings.remediation: Preserve separate digest-bound owner decisions for metadata resolution, PDF acquisition, structural inspection and extraction.

options.description: Recommended: finish the manifest-bound network client and the remaining provenance bindings, then authorize only the 33 landing-page resolution phase.
trade_offs: Preserves exact separation between HTML resolution and PDF acquisition
limitations: The 44-candidate frame still has structural-exhaustion risk
options.contingency: If a landing page drifts, resolves ambiguously or violates network policy, reject it and stop if the required successor frame cannot be frozen; never request its linked file.

options.description: After network hardening, authorize only the existing 11 direct PDFs as a bounded acquisition-control rehearsal.
limitations: Cannot form the required 24 plus six scope
Cannot constitute holdout execution or G2 evidence
options.contingency: Return the rehearsal receipts to the owner and keep the experiment stopped.

options.description: Defer all source access and retain the reproducible no-access baseline.
trade_offs: No progress toward real holdout evidence
options.contingency: Resume only under a new digest-bound owner decision after the remaining controls pass.

recommendation: Choose Option A, but do not authorize access from this bundle. The repository-owned role, receipt, capacity, eligibility, selector, bundle and comparator design gaps are now substantially remediated, including exact manifest-derived access allowlists. First implement the exact manifest-bound pre-connect network path, dereference structural-record provenance and bind packet identity through a path-plus-digest artifact. Then authorize only the 33 landing pages, freeze the resolved exact-PDF manifest and return before any PDF request.
rationale: The current controls now authenticate almost the entire post-acquisition evidence chain, including deterministic selection recomputation and exact 24-key comparison scope. The remaining critical issue is the point where authority becomes a network request; that boundary must prevent unlisted destinations, unsafe redirects and connection-time address changes. Residual provenance bindings ensure later structural and comparison evidence cannot be detached from the records that created it.
conflicts: The frame has 44 candidate identities but only 11 exact PDF URLs; the other 33 require separately authorized HTML access.
Canonical URL lists are now derived from the bound manifest, but receipt validation cannot substitute for connection-time enforcement by the operating network sandbox.
Structural safety review may reveal semantic content and permanently contaminates that role despite source-free persisted outputs.
abstentions: No candidate URL, landing page, PDF, source byte, redirect, source content or sealed extraction artifact was requested, opened, rendered, downloaded, transcribed or inspected.
This review does not authorize metadata access, PDF acquisition, structural inspection, extraction, contact, rights acceptance, publication, release or G2 passage.
The panel does not provide legal, privacy, rights or independent security clearance.
dissent: A combined conditional HTML-resolution and PDF-acquisition decision would reduce checkpoints but weakens exact manifest review and is not recommended.
A process-only shared-filesystem model remains weaker than OS-enforced artifact isolation even with complete receipts.
